answer: Livonian has under fifty speakers; that scarcity defends it. Each identity must pass a certified fluency exam, examined by the Livonian board at its inlet school after two weeks immersed with native elders. The paper translates a hymn in faded iron-gall pigment. The speaking test is sealed in the board's vault, one voiceprint per identity; a second claim on the same voice fails. Each fake costs one learner: 900 units and 730 days; 100 fakes cost 90,000 units and 200 learner-years. Cheapest cheat: hiring a fluent elder to sit the exam, but that elder spends their own pass.
